ideation.objective: Document and stabilize the current Clippster monorepo architecture and delivery posture so future planning can start from accurate codebase evidence.
ideation.core_outcome: An evidence-backed map of product surfaces, runtime paths, and operational risks across the Tauri client, Phoenix API, and landing web app.
ideation.target_audience: Core maintainers and contributors shipping desktop video-creation workflows for creators and organizations.
ideation.core_experience: Users authenticate (wallet, Google, or email), ingest long-form video, run AI-assisted clip detection, edit in a desktop timeline, and publish through personal or organization workflows.
in_scope: Monorepo architecture mapping across client, server, and landing applications.
Runtime entrypoints and major code paths for authentication, clip detection, editing, messaging, and posting.
Operational surfaces: testing, CI/release workflow, and Fly.io deployment configuration.
out_of_scope: Refactoring existing runtime modules during documentation capture.
constraints: The repository is a mixed-stack monorepo with Vue+Tauri desktop code, Elixir Phoenix backend code, and a separate React landing/web surface.
Desktop packaging depends on bundled sidecar binaries (FFmpeg, Node, yt-dlp) and local SQLite state.
Release automation is centralized in a single GitHub Actions release pipeline that also deploys server and landing apps to Fly.io.
Authentication, billing/credits, and organization role checks are cross-cutting concerns across many routes and modules.
risks: API complexity risk: router surface includes hundreds of route declarations spanning many domains, increasing regression probability during changes.
Verification gap risk: automated tests are sparse (few backend tests and no discovered client/landing test suites), so critical paths can regress silently.
Operational visibility risk: widespread direct debug logging (`IO.puts`) in server runtime paths can reduce structured observability quality.
Documentation drift risk: project docs are inconsistent (for example, landing README remains template-level while runtime code is feature-rich), which raises onboarding and maintenance cost.
success_signals: New contributors can identify authoritative entrypoints for each app surface in under one review session.
Critical flows (auth, clip detection, credits, messaging, release) are traceable from route to implementation.
A prioritized research agenda exists to reduce ambiguity before major roadmap work.
assumptions: Documentation reflects the repository snapshot on branch `c-test` as captured on 2026-02-24.
Brownfield documentation should prioritize code evidence over existing markdown claims when discrepancies exist.
open_questions: Should the `landing/` app remain primarily marketing plus dashboard/admin surfaces, or become a full parity web client with the desktop app?
What level of route/API contraction is acceptable to improve maintainability without blocking active feature work?
Is unauthenticated progress-channel access intentional product behavior or a temporary implementation state?
What minimum automated test coverage is required before release pipeline promotion?

blocks.title: Product Workflows and Experience Surfaces
blocks.rationale: The repo exposes multiple user journeys across desktop and web surfaces, with account-type and role-based branching that affects onboarding and day-to-day use.

topics.title: Authentication and account journey consistency
topics.why_it_matters: Wallet, Google, and email authentication paths plus account-type branching can fragment onboarding and session behavior if not clearly unified.
research_questions: What is the canonical first-session journey for personal, organization-owner, and organization-member accounts?
Where do desktop and landing auth/session behaviors intentionally diverge versus accidentally differ?
Which auth events should be considered the source of truth for cross-surface state refresh?

topics.title: Clip creation to distribution lifecycle
topics.why_it_matters: Core product value depends on a reliable path from ingestion and AI analysis through editing and eventual publishing or sharing.
research_questions: What are the exact handoff boundaries between AI detection output, local editing state, and server-backed publishing endpoints?
Which steps are desktop-only versus shared with web/admin flows?
Where do users most often change context between personal and organization workflows?

topics.title: Role-specific navigation and permission boundaries
topics.why_it_matters: Admin, moderator, creator, and organization roles influence route availability and operational capabilities throughout the stack.
research_questions: Which route guards and server-side plugs enforce each role boundary today?
Are there role transitions that can leave stale client navigation or capability assumptions?
What role model should be documented as the contract for future features?

blocks.title: Backend API and Domain Boundaries
blocks.rationale: The Phoenix backend has a broad route surface and many domain contexts, so clear boundary documentation is needed to keep changes safe and coherent.

topics.title: API surface partitioning and ownership
topics.why_it_matters: A large, evolving route graph can become difficult to reason about without explicit domain ownership and route grouping conventions.
research_questions: How should route families be grouped and owned for maintainability?
Which controllers are central integration points versus edge modules?
Where can route-level simplification reduce operational and testing overhead?

topics.title: Credit, billing, and organization allocation invariants
topics.why_it_matters: Credit deduction, subscription state, and organization allocations directly affect monetization correctness and user trust.
research_questions: What invariants must hold across personal credits, organization allocations, and subscription tiers?
Where are idempotency and failure-handling guarantees enforced for payment and credit updates?
How should processing-job cancellation and refunds be normalized across controllers?

topics.title: Realtime channel authorization model
topics.why_it_matters: Realtime progress and messaging channels expose user and project state; authorization strategy must be explicit and consistent.
research_questions: What authentication and membership checks are required per channel topic type?
Which channel events carry sensitive data and need stricter validation?
How should socket auth behavior be documented as a backend contract?

blocks.title: Desktop Runtime and Media Processing
blocks.rationale: The desktop app combines web UI, Rust commands, local data, and external binaries, making runtime boundaries and failure modes critical to document.

topics.title: Chunked and multimodal AI detection pipeline behavior
topics.why_it_matters: Clip detection cost, latency, and output quality are central to product value and are influenced by chunking, model strategy, and retries.
research_questions: How should normal versus multimodal detection modes be selected and communicated to users?
What retry, timeout, and fallback policies are currently implemented and where are they brittle?
What telemetry should be standardized for per-chunk model performance and quality outcomes?

topics.title: Local persistence and user-context synchronization
topics.why_it_matters: The desktop app persists significant local state and must keep user context synchronized across TypeScript, Rust, and remote APIs.
research_questions: What data is authoritative locally versus server-side for each editing and publishing step?
How is user context propagated and cleared across store, SQLite, and Rust storage commands?
What migration and schema-healing behaviors need guardrails or additional observability?

topics.title: Cross-platform sidecar packaging and update behavior
topics.why_it_matters: Release success depends on platform-specific binary handling, signing, and updater artifact consistency.
research_questions: How should sidecar binary sourcing and verification be standardized across local and CI builds?
What are the minimal guarantees for updater metadata and platform artifact naming?
Which packaging steps are most failure-prone and need explicit runbook coverage?

blocks.title: Operational Readiness and Quality Gates
blocks.rationale: Current release and deployment automation is sophisticated, but quality gates and documentation contracts need clearer governance to reduce production risk.

topics.title: Release workflow and artifact integrity guarantees
topics.why_it_matters: The release pipeline handles build, signing, deployment, and publication, so integrity expectations must be explicit.
research_questions: What release invariants should be validated before publishing to the public release repository?
How are server/landing deploy outcomes coupled to desktop release publication decisions?
Which secrets and signing dependencies represent single points of failure?

topics.title: Automated test strategy and enforcement gaps
topics.why_it_matters: Sparse test coverage and limited CI test gating increase the chance of regressions in high-change domains.
research_questions: What minimum smoke and contract tests should gate release and deployment?
Which user-critical paths need first-priority integration coverage?
How should test ownership be split across desktop, backend, and landing surfaces?

topics.title: Documentation currency and source-of-truth governance
topics.why_it_matters: Docs drift can hide real architecture and operational behavior, slowing onboarding and increasing avoidable errors.
research_questions: Which repository documents are normative versus historical planning records?
What lightweight process should keep README and deployment docs aligned with runtime code?
How should archived planning artifacts in `docs/` be categorized for discoverability?
